audit_findings.title: Equity-method investments may be counted both in owner earnings and the valuation bridge
audit_findings.mechanism: Equity-method earnings or distributions may remain in OE while $4.602 billion of stakes is added separately in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Equity earnings (losses) in the Consolidated Statement of Income includes Williams’ allocable share of net income (loss) of investees adjusted for any depreciation and amortization, as applicable, associated with basis differences.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved but materially scaled possibility, not a demonstrated double count without the OE workpaper. The filing reports $760 million of 2025 equity earnings and $800 million of distributions from equity-method investees, compared with $2.0005 billion of anchor OE and a $4.602 billion stakes addition. Capitalizing any retained stake-derived earnings and then adding the investments could materially overstate value.
audit_findings.action: Trace the 2025 OE calculation investee by investee through equity earnings, basis-difference amortization, distributions, contributions and related operating fees; rerun after either purging all stake economics from OE or excluding the corresponding stakes from the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Parent earnings are mixed with consolidated cash-flow adjustments despite material NCI
audit_findings.mechanism: Parent-attributable income is combined with 100 percent consolidated D&A, working-capital movements and capital spending before division by parent common shares.
audit_findings.evidence: Williams owns a 65 percent interest in the Northeast JV, a subsidiary that is a VIE due to certain voting rights being disproportionate to the obligation to absorb losses and substantially all of the Northeast JV’s activities being performed on Williams’ behalf.
audit_findings.explanation: The mixed perimeter is demonstrated if the described OE construction was used, but the net correction cannot be established from the record because NCI shares of each add-back and deduction are absent. Consolidated D&A add-backs attributable to NCI overstate parent OE, while consolidated capital and working-capital deductions attributable to NCI understate it. The scale is material: 2025 NCI income was $150 million, NCI distributions were $259 million and NCI equity was $2.188 billion; the July 2026 sale of 49 percent of five power projects adds further prospective NCI complexity.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild every historical and forecast year on one perimeter: either parent-attributable OE with each NCI portion removed, or consolidated OE followed by an explicit deduction for the NCI claim, distributions and project economics; incorporate the new power-project NCI before rerunning.

audit_findings.title: Scenario growth may be capitalized without paying for the required reinvestment
audit_findings.mechanism: The DCF applies 3 percent and 5 percent growth to OE without an explicit project-level deduction for the incremental construction spending and capital contributions producing that growth.
audit_findings.evidence: Williams’ growth capital and investment expenditures in 2026 are expected to range from $6.1 billion to $6.7 billion, as previously discussed in Company Outlook.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated modeling gap unless the scenario workpapers contain an undisclosed reinvestment schedule. The latest filing increased expected 2026 growth capital and investment expenditures to $7.3-$7.9 billion, versus anchor OE of $2.0005 billion, while reported RONTA is only 5.7 percent against a 10 percent required return. The exact value correction is unquantified because the record does not separate funded growth spending, customer reimbursements, NCI funding, timing and resulting incremental OE.
audit_findings.action: Rerun each scenario with annual project-specific capital expenditures and equity-method contributions, customer reimbursements and NCI-funded portions, in-service dates and incremental parent OE; reconcile the schedule to the $7.3-$7.9 billion 2026 outlook and the July 2026 power-project financing.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may retain a nonrecurring Cogentrix fair-value gain
audit_findings.magnitude: $153 million pre-tax, equal to 7.6% of anchor OE; if fully embedded, approximately $2.15 billion or $1.71 per share of base operating value before tax or basis adjustments
audit_findings.mechanism: A one-time equity-method fair-value gain may inflate the latest-actual OE anchor and therefore every forecast year and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: During the fourth quarter of 2025, Williams recorded $ 153 million of Equity earnings (losses) from Cogentrix, primarily reflecting the favorable impact to fair value of an announced agreement to sell a significant portion of the underlying power plant assets.
audit_findings.explanation: The $153 million Cogentrix gain is demonstrated and transaction-driven, but its retention in OE remains unresolved without the anchor reconciliation. Its scale is material because the model uses 2025 OE as the permanent anchor. The latest 10-Q also says Cogentrix's carrying value continues to reflect the announced-sale fair-value uplift. Removal is unnecessary only if all Cogentrix economics were already purged under the separate-stakes treatment.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile Cogentrix's full $153 million gain, related operating expenses, taxes and basis adjustments to 2025 OE; if retained, remove the nonrecurring amount and rerun all scenarios, or document its elimination through the broader stake purge.

audit_findings.title: Capitalized interest can escape an equity-level OE calculation
audit_findings.magnitude: $62 million, equal to 3.1% of anchor OE and approximately $0.69 per share of base value before tax effects
audit_findings.mechanism: Interest embedded in excluded growth capital may be absent from both current interest expense and the OE capital deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: Interest capitalized was $ 62 million, $ 68 million, and $ 54 million in 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates $62 million of capitalized interest in 2025, but the record does not establish whether it was separately deducted from OE. Even assuming the entire amount escaped and directly reduced the anchor, the computed base-value effect is about $0.69 per share, or 2.6 percent of the $26.17 base value, and cannot bridge the $47.88 gap to the $74.05 market price. Future amounts could be larger during the build program, but that prospective exposure is not presently quantified.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the 2025 OE reconciliation includes the $62 million whenever associated growth capital was excluded; separately forecast capitalized interest for the construction program and rerun if its annual effect becomes materially larger.

audit_findings.title: Preferred dividends sit ahead of the common-share denominator
audit_findings.magnitude: $3 million annually, equal to 0.15% of anchor OE and approximately $0.03 per share of base value
audit_findings.mechanism: OE attributable to all parent equity may be divided by common shares without first deducting the preferred dividend or otherwise recognizing the preferred claim.
audit_findings.evidence: Diluted earnings (loss) per common share may also include any dilutive effect of Williams’ preferred stock.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing correctly presents $2.618 billion of parent-attributable 2025 income, deducts $3 million of preferred dividends and reports $2.615 billion available to common; whether the OE workpaper followed that presentation is unresolved. If omitted, the $3 million annual claim changes base value by only about $0.03 per share. The $35 million recorded preferred balance is also only about $0.03 per common share, so neither treatment could alter the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Verify that each OE year starts from income available to common or explicitly deducts the $3 million preferred dividend; confirm the forecast maintains the deduction and does not also subtract the preferred claim in the bridge.
